## Purpose

This statement defines the boundaries and applicability of the information security management system (ISMS) of PaketPort Group as required by ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 4.3. It is generated from the organisation register so that the scope, the entity ids used in every document's `applies_to` field and the per-entity Statements of Applicability can never drift apart.

## The organisation

PaketPort designs, installs and operates street-sited parcel lockers and the cloud platform behind them: a customer app, a parcel-routing and slot-allocation engine, carrier API integrations and a fleet-management plane that delivers signed firmware over the air to the Linux edge devices in the lockers. The group consists of the Austrian parent, which runs the platform and the Austrian locker estate, a German sales and field-service subsidiary that operates a growing German estate, and a Czech development centre. The ISMS was first certified for the Austrian entity and is being rolled out to the German and Czech entities under a single group certificate.

**Sector.** Parcel-locker logistics — postal and courier services (NIS2 essential entity in Austria)

## External and internal issues (clause 4.1)

### External issues

- NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) classifies the Austrian parent as an essential entity; the German subsidiary is expected to qualify as an important entity under the national transposition.
- The Cyber Resilience Act brings product-security and vulnerability-handling obligations for the locker hardware and firmware as products with digital elements.
- Carrier partners require contractual security assurances, API availability commitments and incident notification, and increasingly ask for certification evidence before onboarding.
- Street-sited lockers are internet-exposed, physically accessible and continuously scanned.
- The platform depends on a single public cloud provider under a shared-responsibility model.
- Operations span three jurisdictions (AT, DE, CZ) with differing labour, privacy and NIS2 transposition rules.

### Internal issues

- A small security function (one ISMS manager, one security engineer) serves the whole group.
- Rapid growth into Germany and Czechia means people, processes and tooling are still converging.
- Three generations of locker hardware with different firmware capabilities are in the field.
- Platform knowledge is concentrated in a few engineers (see risk R-013).
- Hybrid working is the norm for office roles; field technicians work entirely off-premises.

## Interfaces and dependencies

| External party | Direction | Description | Governed by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Carrier partners | bidirectional | Label, tracking and handover-event exchange over authenticated APIs; carriers also receive incident notifications under their contracts. | LEG-05, POL-SUP, POL-NET |
| Public cloud provider | bidirectional | Hosting of the backend, data stores and tooling. The provider's physical infrastructure is outside the scope and covered by its own certifications under the shared-responsibility model. | LEG-07, POL-SUP |
| Locker hardware manufacturer | inbound | Supplies enclosures, controllers and spare parts; firmware components are integrated and signed by PaketPort. | POL-SUP, POL-SDLC |
| Payment service provider | outbound | Hosted payment pages and tokenised payments for the customer app; card data never touches PaketPort systems. | POL-SUP |
| Retail and municipal site hosts | inbound | Provide locker sites, power and sometimes network uplinks; site staff have no access to the locker enclosure or systems. | POL-PHY |
| NIS2 competent authorities and CSIRTs | outbound | Registration, incident early warnings, notifications and final reports under Art. 23, and responses to supervisory requests. | PROC-IR, LEG-01 |
| PaketPort Italia S.r.l. (reseller joint venture) | inbound | Out-of-scope reseller with partner-portal access only; treated as a supplier-type relationship. | POL-SUP |
| Field-service subcontractors (Germany) | inbound | Vetted subcontractors with time-limited access to maintenance tooling for the German estate. | POL-SUP, PROC-JML |

## Exclusions and their justification

| Id | Excluded item | Justification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ENT-IT | PaketPort Italia S.r.l. | PaketPort holds 40 % and exercises no management control over the joint venture's processes or IT. The only interface is the partner portal, which is governed by the reseller agreement and treated as a third-party relationship under POL-SUP. Bringing the entity into scope would require contractual rights PaketPort does not have. |
| SITE-MIL-OFFICE | Milan reseller office | Office of the out-of-scope joint venture PaketPort Italia S.r.l.; no group systems or data are processed there beyond partner-portal access. |

The physical infrastructure of the public cloud provider and the internal systems of carriers, suppliers and site hosts are outside the scope; the interfaces to them are listed above and governed by the documents named there.
